# Package servers in ezupdate

This page is for administrators who want an installed site to see the packages of more than one `.ezpkg` package
server: the 7x server, a server of their own, an agency's. ezupdate keeps that list on its **Package servers** page
and on the command line. It is a list for browsing and fetching, and from Exponential 6.0.15 on the setup wizard, the
kickstarter and `exp:install` read it too, after the server of `package.ini`.

## Contents

1. [Open the page](#open-the-page)
2. [The built-in server](#the-built-in-server)
3. [Add a server](#add-a-server)
4. [Remove a server](#remove-a-server)
5. [From the command line](#from-the-command-line)
6. [What the list is used for](#what-the-list-is-used-for)

## Open the page

**Setup > Updates and packages**, tab **Package servers** (`/update/servers`).

![The Package servers tab of Updates and packages: the Composer servers list with packagist.org switched on and a form to add a server, and the Exponential package servers list with the built-in server exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15](../../images/site-packages-ezupdate-servers.webp)

The page has two lists:

| Section | Holds | Kept in |
|---|---|---|
| Composer servers | where Composer looks for code packages: the `repositories` of `composer.json` | `composer.json` |
| Exponential package servers | "Servers of .ezpkg packages (site designs, content classes, demo content), in the index.xml format the setup wizard reads." | `settings/override/ezupdate.ini.append.php` |

This page is about the second list. The page needs the policy `update/manage` (`extension/ezupdate/modules/update/module.php`);
ezupdate is switched on with `ActiveExtensions[]=ezupdate` ([ezupdate: updates and packages in the admin](../../../features/6.0/extensions/ezupdate.md)).

## The built-in server

The first row is always the server the setup wizard uses, named `exponential` and marked **built in** (title
`package.ini`). ezupdate resolves it the way the wizard does (`eZUpdatePackageServers::builtinIndexURL()`):
`package.ini [RepositorySettings] RemotePackagesIndexURL`, or, when that is empty, `RemotePackagesIndexURLBase` with
`x.y/x.y.z` appended (`6.0/6.0.15`; before ezupdate 1.1.24 it appended `6.0/6.0.15stable`, a folder the package
server does not have). On a default 6.0.15 installation that is
`https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15`.

It cannot be removed here and its name is reserved: change it in `package.ini` (an override) if it must change
([Pointing a site at your package server](../your-own/pointing-a-site-at-your-package-server.md)).

## Add a server

Under **Add package server**, give a **Name** and an **Address** and submit.

| Field | Rule (`eZUpdatePackageServers::validate()`) | Message on failure |
|---|---|---|
| Name | letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters | "The name may use letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore." |
| Name | not `exponential` | "This name is reserved for the server in package.ini." |
| Address | an `https://` URL | "The address must be an https:// URL." |

The address is the folder that holds `index.xml`, without `/index.xml` and without a trailing slash (one is removed),
for example `https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15`. Adding a name that exists replaces its address.
On success the page says "The package server was added."

The server is written to the override file:

```ini
<?php /* #?ini charset="utf-8"?
[PackageServerSettings]
Servers[acme]=https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15
*/ ?>
```

If the file cannot be written, the page says "Could not write settings/override/ezupdate.ini.append.php." The file is
read directly, without the INI cache, so the page and the command line always show the same list.

## Remove a server

**Remove** on a row asks "Remove this package server?" and deletes its line from the override file ("The package
server was removed."). Packages already fetched from it stay in the local repository.

## From the command line

```bash
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php servers
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php server-add ezpkg acme https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php server-remove ezpkg acme
```

`servers` lists both kinds; the built-in one is shown with `(package.ini)`. The same rules apply as on the page
(`extension/ezupdate/doc/COMMAND_LINE.md`).

## What the list is used for

| Used by | For |
|---|---|
| ezupdate's **Packages** page and `packages` command | listing a server's packages |
| ezupdate's **Fetch** and `fetch` command | downloading one into the local repository |
| the setup wizard, the kickstarter, `exp:install` | from 6.0.15 on: further servers, read after `package.ini`'s (`[RepositorySettings] RemotePackagesIndexSources[]=ezupdate.ini;PackageServerSettings;Servers`, the default). Before 6.0.15 they read only `package.ini [RepositorySettings]` |

So adding a server here lets administrators fetch its packages into an installed site, and the setup tools of the same
installation offer its site packages next to those of the `package.ini` server (a package both list is taken from the
`package.ini` server). For a new installation, which has no ezupdate list yet,
point `package.ini` at the server (`RemotePackagesIndexURL`, or `AdditionalRemotePackagesIndexURLs[]` to keep the
7x server too), or submit the packages to the 7x server
([Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md)).

> **Note**
> With `site.ini [ConfigurationSettings] ManagedByDeployment=enabled`, settings files are not written from a web
> request, so adding or removing a server in the browser fails; keep the list in the deployment instead.
